chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What is the spatial geometry and bond angle around the central carbon in methane (CH₄)?

options.label: A
options.text: Tetrahedral geometry with ideal bond angles of 109.5° resulting from sp³ hybridization.

options.label: B
options.text: Trigonal planar geometry with 120° angles.

options.label: C
options.text: Square planar geometry with 90° angles.

options.label: D
options.text: Linear geometry with 180° angles.

questions.correct_answer: Tetrahedral geometry with ideal bond angles of 109.5° resulting from sp³ hybridization.
questions.explanation: Methane has 4 steric electron domains with zero lone pairs, giving a regular tetrahedral geometry with 109.5° bond angles.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Why is the bond angle in ammonia (NH₃, 107.3°) smaller than the ideal tetrahedral angle (109.5°)?

options.label: A
options.text: Ammonia is an sp² hybridized planar molecule.

options.label: B
options.text: Nitrogen has an expanded octet.

options.label: C
options.text: The unshared sp³ lone pair exerts greater electron-electron repulsion, compressing the adjacent N-H bonding pairs.

options.label: D
options.text: Hydrogen atoms attract each other via ionic bonding.

questions.correct_answer: The unshared sp³ lone pair exerts greater electron-electron repulsion, compressing the adjacent N-H bonding pairs.
questions.explanation: Nonbonding lone pairs are physically larger and more diffuse than bonding pairs, exerting greater repulsion and compressing bonding angles.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Water Bent Geometry and Dipole Moment
questions.question: Why does water (H₂O) have a permanent net dipole moment (1.85 D) whereas carbon dioxide (CO₂) has zero dipole moment?

options.label: A
options.text: Water has a bent geometry (104.5°) with two polar O-H bond dipoles that add vectorially, whereas linear CO₂ has two equal bond dipoles that cancel exactly.

options.label: B
options.text: Oxygen is more electronegative in CO₂ than in water.

options.label: C
options.text: CO₂ contains single bonds exclusively.

options.label: D
options.text: Water has no lone pairs on oxygen.

questions.correct_answer: Water has a bent geometry (104.5°) with two polar O-H bond dipoles that add vectorially, whereas linear CO₂ has two equal bond dipoles that cancel exactly.
questions.explanation: Vector summation of bond dipoles in bent H₂O produces a strong net molecular dipole, whereas in linear CO₂ the vectors cancel.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What is the formal charge on the oxygen atom in the hydronium cation (H₃O⁺)?

options.label: A
options.text: +1 formal charge (6 valence electrons - 2 nonbonding electrons - 3 bonding electrons = +1).

options.label: B
options.text: +2 formal charge.

options.label: C
options.text: 0 formal charge.

options.label: D
options.text: -1 formal charge.

questions.correct_answer: +1 formal charge (6 valence electrons - 2 nonbonding electrons - 3 bonding electrons = +1).
questions.explanation: Formal charge = Valence - (Nonbonding + 1/2 Bonding) = 6 - (2 + 3) = +1.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What is the hybridization and bond angle around the carbonyl carbon in acetone [(CH₃)₂C=O]?

options.label: A
options.text: dsp³ hybridization with 90° angles.

options.label: B
options.text: sp hybridization with linear 180° geometry.

options.label: C
options.text: sp² hybridization with trigonal planar geometry and approximately 120° bond angles.

options.label: D
options.text: sp³ hybridization with 109.5° tetrahedral angles.

questions.correct_answer: sp² hybridization with trigonal planar geometry and approximately 120° bond angles.
questions.explanation: The carbonyl carbon has 3 steric domains (2 C-C σ bonds, 1 C=O σ bond) with zero lone pairs, dictated by sp² hybridization.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Ethylene Planar Geometry and Pi Bond
questions.question: Why are all six atoms of ethylene (H₂C=CH₂) constrained to lie in the exact same geometric plane?

options.label: A
options.text: The carbon-carbon bond rotates freely at room temperature.

options.label: B
options.text: Sideways overlap of the two unhybridized 2p orbitals forming the π bond requires parallel alignment of both sp² carbon planes.

options.label: C
options.text: Ethylene is an aromatic ring.

options.label: D
options.text: C-H bonds repel each other into a circle.

questions.correct_answer: Sideways overlap of the two unhybridized 2p orbitals forming the π bond requires parallel alignment of both sp² carbon planes.
questions.explanation: Rotation around the C=C double bond is restricted by the π bond (~260 kJ/mol barrier), locking all 6 atoms in a single coplanar framework.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What is the hybridization and spatial arrangement of carbons in propyne (CH₃-C≡C-H)?

options.label: A
options.text: The methyl carbon is sp³ tetrahedral; the two alkyne carbons are sp linear (180° bond angle).

options.label: B
options.text: All three carbons are sp³ tetrahedral.

options.label: C
options.text: The alkyne carbons are sp² bent.

options.label: D
options.text: All three carbons are sp² trigonal planar.

questions.correct_answer: The methyl carbon is sp³ tetrahedral; the two alkyne carbons are sp linear (180° bond angle).
questions.explanation: The terminal alkyne carbons have 2 steric domains (180°, sp), while the saturated methyl carbon has 4 steric domains (109.5°, sp³).

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: In the Lewis structure of the amine oxide (CH₃)₃N⁺-O⁻, what is the nature of the nitrogen-oxygen bond?

options.label: A
options.text: A nonpolar N=O double bond with expanded octet on nitrogen.

options.label: B
options.text: A hydrogen bond between methyl and oxygen.

options.label: C
options.text: A purely ionic bond with no electron sharing.

options.label: D
options.text: A highly polarized coordinate covalent single bond with formal charges of +1 on nitrogen and -1 on oxygen.

questions.correct_answer: A highly polarized coordinate covalent single bond with formal charges of +1 on nitrogen and -1 on oxygen.
questions.explanation: Nitrogen cannot expand its valence shell to 10 electrons (period 2); the N-O bond is a single coordinate bond with +1/-1 formal charges.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Why is the boiling point of ethanol (78°C) dramatically higher than that of its constitutional isomer dimethyl ether (-24°C)?

options.label: A
options.text: Ethanol has a higher molecular weight than dimethyl ether.

options.label: B
options.text: Ethanol molecules form strong intermolecular O-H···O hydrogen bonding networks, whereas dimethyl ether has only weaker dipole-dipole interactions.

options.label: C
options.text: Ethanol has a nonpolar linear structure.

options.label: D
options.text: Dimethyl ether is an ionic solid at room temperature.

questions.correct_answer: Ethanol molecules form strong intermolecular O-H···O hydrogen bonding networks, whereas dimethyl ether has only weaker dipole-dipole interactions.
questions.explanation: Intermolecular hydrogen bonding in alcohols requires substantial thermal energy to overcome, elevating boiling points.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Which of the following bonds possesses the greatest individual bond dipole moment?

options.label: C
options.text: C-F bond (electronegativity difference ΔEN = 4.0 - 2.5 = 1.5).

options.label: D
options.text: C-C bond (ΔEN = 0.0).

questions.correct_answer: C-F bond (electronegativity difference ΔEN = 4.0 - 2.5 = 1.5).
questions.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element in the periodic table, creating the largest polarization and bond dipole with carbon.

questions.question: Why does water (H₂O) have a permanent net dipole moment (1.85 D) whereas carbon dioxide (CO₂) has zero dipole moment?

options.label: A
options.text: CO₂ contains single bonds exclusively.

options.label: B
options.text: Water has a bent geometry (104.5°) with two polar O-H bond dipoles that add vectorially, whereas linear CO₂ has two equal bond dipoles that cancel exactly.

options.label: C
options.text: Oxygen is more electronegative in CO₂ than in water.

options.label: D
options.text: Water has no lone pairs on oxygen.

questions.correct_answer: Water has a bent geometry (104.5°) with two polar O-H bond dipoles that add vectorially, whereas linear CO₂ has two equal bond dipoles that cancel exactly.
questions.explanation: Vector summation of bond dipoles in bent H₂O produces a strong net molecular dipole, whereas in linear CO₂ the vectors cancel.
